chapter.title: Phrasal Verbs
chapter.description: Learn common English phrasal verbs formed by combining verbs with prepositions or adverbs, focusing on general sentence usage and specific verbs like 'look', 'come', and 'get'.

rules.title: What is a Phrasal Verb?
rules.explanation: A phrasal verb is a combination of a verb and a particle (a preposition or adverb) that creates a new meaning different from the original verb itself (e.g., 'look after' means 'to take care of').
rules.example: Please look after my dog while I am away.

rules.title: Separable vs. Inseparable Phrasal Verbs
rules.explanation: Some phrasal verbs can be separated by the object (e.g., 'turn the lights off' or 'turn off the lights'). If the object is a pronoun, it MUST go between the verb and particle (e.g., 'turn it off'). Inseparable phrasal verbs keep the verb and particle together (e.g., 'look for something').
rules.example: Turn off the TV. / Turn it off. (NOT: Turn off it.)

rules.title: Phrasal Verbs with 'Look'
rules.explanation: Common phrasal verbs with 'look' include: 'look for' (search), 'look after' (care for), 'look forward to' (anticipate with pleasure), 'look up' (search for information), and 'look out' (be careful).
rules.example: I am looking for my keys. / Look out! A car is coming.

rules.title: Phrasal Verbs with 'Come' and 'Get'
rules.explanation: 'Come across' (find by chance), 'come up with' (invent/suggest an idea), 'get on/along with' (have a good relationship), 'get over' (recover from), and 'get away' (escape).
rules.example: She came across an old photo. / They get on well together.

questions.question: Can you ____ the lights when you leave the room?
questions.explanation: 'Turn off' means to stop an electrical device or light from operating.

questions.question: Don't ____! I know you can solve this puzzle if you keep trying.
questions.explanation: 'Give up' means to stop trying or surrender.

questions.question: The plane will ____ in about ten minutes.
questions.explanation: 'Take off' means to leave the ground and begin to fly.

questions.question: They had to ____ the outdoor concert because of the heavy rain.
questions.explanation: 'Call off' means to cancel an event.

questions.question: Please ____ this application form with your personal details.
questions.explanation: 'Fill in' means to complete a form or document by adding information.

questions.sentence: I need to ________ my lost wallet. Have you seen it?
questions.explanation: 'Look for' means to search for something.

questions.sentence: Could you ________ my cat while I am on vacation?
questions.explanation: 'Look after' means to take care of someone or something.

questions.sentence: I am really ________ seeing you at the weekend party!
questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' means to feel excited about something that is going to happen.

questions.sentence: If you don't know the meaning of the word, ________ it in the dictionary.
questions.explanation: 'Look up' means to search for information in a reference book or online.
'Look out' is used as a warning to be careful.

questions.sentence: I ________ an old childhood photograph while cleaning my room.
questions.explanation: 'Come across' means to find something by chance.

questions.sentence: She ________ a great idea for our science project.
questions.explanation: 'Come up with' means to think of or produce an idea/plan.

questions.sentence: What time will you ________ home tonight?
questions.explanation: 'Come back' means to return to a place.

questions.sentence: The new album will ________ next month.
questions.explanation: 'Come out' means to be published, released, or made available to the public.

questions.sentence: Please ________ and take a seat; the door is open.
questions.explanation: 'Come in' means to enter a room or building.

questions.question: Do you ____ well with your new neighbors?
questions.explanation: 'Get along' (or 'get on') means to have a good relationship with someone.

questions.question: It took him a long time to ____ the flu.
questions.explanation: 'Get over' means to recover from an illness or emotional disappointment.

questions.question: What time do you usually ____ in the morning?
questions.explanation: 'Get up' means to rise from bed after sleeping.

questions.question: We need to ____ at the next bus stop.
questions.explanation: 'Get off' means to leave a bus, train, aircraft, or boat.

questions.question: They want to ____ for the weekend and go to the beach.
questions.explanation: 'Get away' means to go on vacation or escape daily routines.
